\section[nacer]{nacer — to be born}

\label{lesson:ES-C497-nacer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to take away, then the Spanish for to fill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: nacer}
\textbf{nacer} — \textquotedblleft{}to be born\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nací en Sevilla.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I was born in Seville.}
\end{quote}

It takes a \emph{z} in the first person present: \emph{nazco}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nacer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nacer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nacer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to take away, then the Spanish for to fill, then say \emph{nacer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does nacer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be born\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[fallecer]{fallecer — to pass away}

\label{lesson:ES-C497-fallecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to fill, then the Spanish for to be born.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fallecer}
\textbf{fallecer} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His grandfather passed away last year.}
\end{quote}

A gentler, more formal word than \emph{morir}.
